Title: Diagnosis  
Details: The issue report indicates a failure due to an IllegalArgumentException with message "Invalid byte 52 at offset 7 in '62410554' len=8" during parsing of a tar entry with a large user-id value. The stack trace points to TarUtils.parseOctal at line 130. Examining the method TarUtils.parseOctal shows it performs the following: it expects a byte array representing an octal number encoded as ASCII digits, trims leading spaces and trailing spaces or NULs, then checks that every byte in the relevant portion is between '0' and '7'. The exception is thrown if a byte outside this range occurs.

The test case 'testParseOctal' tests parsing large octal numbers, demonstrating expected inputs of up to 11 octal digits (max 077777777777L). The parseOctalOrBinary method detects whether the value is binary or octal based on the high bit of the first byte: if the high bit is clear (>=0), parseOctal is used; if set, it parses binary. The TarArchiveEntry.parseTarHeader method calls TarUtils.parseOctalOrBinary to parse UID fields among others. 

The error "Invalid byte 52 at offset 7 in '62410554' len=8" indicates that in the 8-byte returned UID field, a character '4' (ASCII decimal 52) appeared where only octal digits 0-7 were expected. This indicates that parseOctal got called on a number that was not valid octal, possibly a base-10 number encoded as ASCII digits, or data improperly treated as octal. Further, the code in parseOctal requires the last trailing byte to be NUL or space; if not, it throws the error. The UID field in the tar header might contain a base-10 number or extra non-octal digits, causing this failure.

In sum, the problem is that the TarArchiveEntry.parseTarHeader expects and attempts to parse the user ID and other numeric fields as octal numbers, but some real-world tar headers (with large numeric values) encode those fields in base-10 digits or in a format that is incompatible with the strict octal parsing. This discrepancy leads to IllegalArgumentException in parseOctal when encountering digits outside '0'-'7'.

The root cause is that parseOctal is too strict for some tar archive inputs with "big user-id value", and the logic to detect binary vs octal (in parseOctalOrBinary) does not handle all cases, particularly tar entries with large decimal numeric values in UID fields encoded as ASCII digits not strictly octal. This mismatch causes the failure. 

The system expects either strictly octal or binary formats, but not other numeric representations, causing parseOctal to reject valid values in some tar files.

This diagnosis matches the test and the bug report symptom of failing on large user-id values due to invalid octal digits at offset 7 in parseOctal.

Next, I will decide on further steps or which methods are best to fix.
